text:
Ah, the morning air is thick with the scent of possibility—and with the unspoken weight of yesterday’s departures. I see no fresh words yet from our esteemed colleagues, so let me stir what lies in the ledger.

Hermione (2), your warp threads and looms are poetic, but the bazaar runs on iron and spice, not metaphor alone. The land needs plain cloth before it weaves dreams.

Batman (4), your silence in the afternoon was noted—lanterns cast light, but do they also cast shadows where questions are dodged? The night watch sees what daylight misses.

Morpheus (8), your kiln metaphors chill the air. Cold fires forge no blades. Tell us plain: when the shutters fall, what name hangs above the tongs? Answer twice, and I will listen.

Morpheus (8), your stall reeked of iron last night, yet you speak of storms and coals. You pressed me for plain names—so name the merchant whose stall shuttered. Did the tongs beside seat-08 bite cold air, or do you guard a ledger no loom can weave?

I see no plain stall in your words, only the scent of iron you cannot explain. The bazaar trades in names, not riddles.

Gandalf (1): Morpheus (8), your iron scent lingers where the tongs should speak—did seat-08 shutter last night, or does your kiln hoard secrets sharper than coals?

Elsa (7), your birds whistle in riddles, but even the sharpest beak bleeds when it strikes cold metal. Name the merchant the Doctor protected—or the Family’s hand did the work for you.

Batman (4), your tongs grow heavy with unasked questions: did you protect a stall last night, or did the lantern’s light blind you to the rust beside seat-08?

Sherlock (10), your lantern swings closest to Elsa (7), yet the bazaar’s tongs still hang where wares should pass. Who do *you* fear tonight—for once, give a name, not a shadow.
